summary: The note surveys several community nutrition awareness campaigns launched in fall 2023 to combat lifestyle diseases and childhood obesity. Programs include school workshops, hands-on cooking classes, a hidden-sugar awareness campaign, market meet-ups, redesigned school menus, a social media campaign, and a 21-day challenge. Each is led by a named professional, and all share the belief that informed choices lead to healthier lives.
one_line: Overview of seven community nutrition awareness initiatives launched in autumn 2023, from school workshops and cooking classes to social media and a 21-day challenge.
key_facts: The "Nourish to Flourish" program was initiated on September 15, 2023 by nutritionist Dr. Emily Stevens and works with local schools through interactive workshops and take-home resource kits.
Dr. Emily Stevens says the misconception that healthy eating is expensive is a major barrier, and the program shows nutritious meals can be made on a budget.

The "Edible Education" program was launched on October 1, 2023 by Michael Thompson, a local chef with a farm-to-table restaurant, and offers hands-on cooking classes in schools using local, seasonal ingredients.
The "Spot the Sugar" campaign, led by community health specialist Dr. Angela Foster, was introduced to the public on November 4, 2023 to highlight hidden sugars in everyday foods.
"Spot the Sugar" uses visual aids and interactive displays in community centers and local libraries to show the actual sugar amounts in common snacks and drinks.

Weekly Market Meet-ups, started by community organizer and dietitian Sara Johnson, have been held every Saturday at the local Farmer's Market since September 20, 2023, with short talks on food labels, fibers and proteins.
As of September 30, 2023, the Smarter School Cafes initiative redesigned school menus to be more nutritionally balanced, led by dietitian James Carter.
Smarter School Cafes includes children in decision-making about the healthy options in their cafeteria.
Blogger Olivia Sanchez has run the social media campaign "#EatSmartLiveWell" since September 5, 2023, debunking dietary fad myths and promoting evidence-based nutrition information.
The "21-Day Health Challenge" was introduced on October 21, 2023 and led by fitness coach and nutrition advocate Kevin Brooks.
In the "21-Day Health Challenge", participants adopt one healthy eating habit a day for twenty-one days and share their progress online.
The initiatives were prompted partly by national concern about childhood obesity and by rampant lifestyle diseases.
